_comment: R24 minimal capability floor. Machine-readable, evidence-oriented. See docs/design/r24-cpp-host-preflight.md section 1. Capability names are drawn exactly from spec/manifest.json's required_capabilities/optional_capabilities vocabulary; this file does not invent new capability names.

generic_manifest_required_capabilities_d.reason: generic manifest marks this required, but the R24 minimal bootstrap floor does not require full help-text parity; the pre-flight's bootstrap suite (docs/design/r24/bootstrap-cases.json) does not include doc_help cases. Must be claimed with real evidence before R24 completion (see docs/design/r24-cpp-host-preflight.md section 12), not before.

generic_manifest_optional_capabilities_m.reason: R20 (open functions / extensible pattern dispatch) is an R24 entry prerequisite per docs/design/r24-cpp-host-preflight.md 'Entry prerequisites'. The generic host manifest treats open_functions as optional because not every host capability floor needs it, but R24 specifically cannot be declared complete without it. Distinguishing generic-optional from R24-mandatory is required by the pre-flight (item 5A).

claim_rules: A capability may only be declared 'supported' in a genia-cpp capabilities response once real implementation exists AND the applicable shared cases in bootstrap-cases.json (or a later evidence-backed expansion) pass deterministically via tools/spec_runner --host.
Every capability not yet implemented MUST be declared 'unsupported' in the capabilities response, never omitted and never partially claimed.

No capability in generic_manifest_optional_capabilities_explicitly_out_of_r24_scope may be declared 'supported' as part of R24 completion evidence; adding one requires a roadmap-level scope change, not an implementation-time decision.
This file must be updated in the same commit as any change to which capability genia-cpp claims support for -- capability growth is never a silent side effect of unrelated implementation work.
